gloss: traditional; old-fashioned; unchanged from the old days

definitions.gloss: traditional; old-fashioned; unchanged from the old days
definitions.explanation: describes something that has remained the same since long ago, preserving its original character without modern changes

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{昔|むかし}ながら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: This town still has an old-fashioned shopping street.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{昔|むかし}ながら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{製法|せいほう}→製法：14038_seihou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{味噌|みそ}→味噌：01037_miso⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}り→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother continues to make miso using the traditional method.

notes:
Almost always used as a pre-noun modifier with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: {昔|むかし}ながらの〜. Carries a positive or nostalgic nuance — it appreciates the preservation of old ways rather than criticizing something as outdated. Very common in food and craft contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昔|むかし}ながら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{味|あじ}→味：00826_aji⟧: traditional taste
- {昔|むかし}ながら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{製法|せいほう}→製法：14038_seihou⟧: traditional manufacturing method
- {昔|むかし}ながら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{町並|まちな}み→町並み：10435_machinami⟧: traditional streetscape
- {昔|むかし}ながら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{暮|く}らし→暮らし：02670_kurashi⟧: traditional way of living
- {昔|むかし}ながら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中華|ちゅうか}そば→中華そば：20539_chuukasoba⟧: old-fashioned Chinese noodles

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{伝統的|でんとうてき}→伝統的：04802_dentouteki⟧: traditional — more formal, often implies cultural heritage preservation
- ⟦{古風|こふう}→古風：11893_kofuu⟧な: old-fashioned — can be positive or negative depending on context
- ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: from long ago — similar but emphasizes the time period rather than unchanged character
- レトロ: retro — loanword, suggests intentional old-fashioned aesthetic

COMMON PATTERNS:
⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧ here means "as it has been" or "remaining in a state." Different from the ⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧ meaning "while doing" (e.g., ⟦{歩|ある}き→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧). This is an archaic use of ⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧ that survives in fixed expressions.
